title: Keyring QR and link triggers: conformance vectors
author: bm

config.notes: A trigger is a hint and confers no authority; nothing here tests what a consumer does after accepting one. Each vector gives input (the scanned, opened or pasted text) and channel (scan unless stated). An accept lists via (oob, url or legacy-json), from (the contact DID), id (the handle, null for the legacy format), exp (unix seconds or null), flow (the registered slug, or null when no hint was given), task (the hint as Type URI, major, minor, or null) and ignored (members the reader did not read: invitation.x, body.x, query.x, legacy.x); a legacy accept also lists callbackUrl. config.now is the reader clock; no vector depends on any other time. ui is derived from reason: update = unknown-flow, unsupported-version; expired = expired; scan-only = wrong-channel; not-ours is outside the spec; invalid = every other reason. Legacy reasons (spec 9): missing-param (a required key is absent), bad-value (a required key has the wrong type or form), callback-not-allowed (callback_url is a string that fails the host or length rules). The OOB container and the URL container are both listed so the container decision (spec 2.3, T1) costs only deleting the groups of the one not chosen: URL vectors are the group valid-url and every vector whose input has a _from parameter; OOB vectors are the rest. The authority tasks.example.org and the slug example-stable are test-only. The URL parameter names (_from, _id, _exp, _type, _tp) are placeholders. Where the legacy format carries an extra key, the expectation is the behaviour of the Keyring release that ignores unknown keys (plan Phase 0); no earlier release does that. Transport hint (spec 1 and 6.2.1): the optional member tp (container Y _tp, names separated by a dot; container X body.tp, an array of strings) lists binding names; a name outside config.transportNames, an empty or repeated name is dropped and reported as tp.<name>; a hint that is not an array of strings (X) is ignored whole and reported as body.tp; the member appears in an accept result only when at least one usable name remains. The hint never rejects a trigger. selectionVectors is a second list with its own shape (the contact's DID document and the wallet's configuration in, a selection outcome out); it tests spec 6.2.1 only and a reader of the trigger need not run it.

selection.unmappedTypes: any other service type, including TSPTransport (reserved, not a verified service type), is not a candidate

outcomes.select: binding and endpoint taken from the DID document; the first request and the reply use that binding
outcomes.reject: nothing is sent; reasons did-document-unverified; callback-not-allowed as in the trigger reader

ui.unreachable: This service can't be reached from your wallet.

selection.notes: The preference order here is a test fixture and says nothing about Keyring's order (plan T7, undecided). DIDComm accept (media types) and the order of services in the document do not select a binding.

vectors.note: keyring:// is the https link with the scheme replaced
a trigger never causes a request, so the host of the link is not checked; trust comes from the contact (from)
the flow hint is optional; the consumer then chooses what its first request is (spec open question T5)
created_time and body.accept are DIDComm members this profile never reads and does not report
a stock camera hands the link over as a deep link, so login is accepted there; the controls are the inviter-signed requester screen and number matching (spec 8.2), not the channel
MAJOR 0 is draft: only the implemented MINORs are accepted
a draft MINOR may break, so 0.2 is not read as 0.1
example-stable is a test-only flow configured at MAJOR 1; a MINOR of a supported MAJOR is accepted
goal_code carries a Type URI, not a bare string: a bare string has no namespace
the consumer accepts a SET of authorities (config.acceptedAuthorities) so a producer can move before every wallet is replaced
a private Type URI form is a different identifier (framework: private and registry URIs are distinct)
static checks come before the clock
at or after expires_time the trigger is not acted on
vta-claim registers expRequired: the offer window is minutes, and the inviter enforces it
vta-claim registers fromMustBeAllowListed
base64url without padding
a trigger carries no task body; an attachment is never read, never dispatched and never ignored silently
unrelated links with a from or id parameter are not triggers: the markers are _oob and _from
the lab enrolment link has no marker, so it is outside this document
the query is after the fragment delimiter, so there is no query to read
no value is percent-decoded
a trigger never causes a fetch; DIDComm _oobid (a GET whose response format DIDComm does not define) is not part of this profile
the value is not percent-decoded

target behaviour from the Keyring release that ignores unknown keys (plan Phase 0). Keyring releases before it reject an extra key (parseAgentHostQr), which is why the Farm keeps the QR frozen until that release ships
callback_url is not a string: a type error, bad-value (spec 9), not a host failure
JSON is QR-only
an unknown name is dropped and reported; the rest of the hint and the trigger stand
no usable name: the member is absent from the result; the trigger is accepted
names are compared as exact strings
a hint that is not an array of strings is ignored as a whole and reported; the trigger is accepted
a trigger defines no endpoint: any such member is unknown, ignored and reported, never used. Selection vectors cover what a wallet then does

selectionVectors.note: document order lists https first; the wallet's own preference (didcomm first) decides
same result when the document order is reversed
the service id is misleading; the type decides
accept lists media types for the message; it does not choose a transport, so https is not preferred because the didcomm service lists a profile
the hint cannot add a candidate
hintBreaksTies is false: the hint orders nothing for this wallet
a TSP-only inviter: no supported binding
a service type the wallet has no binding for
the https binding's serviceEndpoint is an https: URL; an http: one is not a candidate
an endpoint offered by the text and absent from the DID document is ignored and never used (spec 6.2.1 rule 7); the document's endpoint is taken
an endpoint in the text that equals the document's is ignored like any other; the document's is taken
the DID document is not verifiable (did:webvh log fails): nothing is sent
the one exception: the legacy Farm callback on an allow-listed host (the contact is the slot DID, vta_did, as in spec 9)
a legacy callback on a host outside the list (the contact is the slot DID, vta_did, as in spec 9)
